title: Chess, But the Locust Í̷̪s̵̈́͂͜ ̶̥̈I̵͖͐̏n̴̈́̀ ̶̀Y̸̲̓͊ő̸̺u̷̗̇̐r̸̗͝ ̴C̵̤͆o̷̮̓͛m̶̧̅p̶͆̀u̴͕̓t̴͇͂e̷͐̈́r̵̒̆
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where, after every full turn (White + Black), there is a 66% chance the Locust appears on a random square. It shows up as a warning for one turn, then on the next turn evaporates that square and any piece still on it for the rest of the game, then disappears to choose a new victim. Deleted squares are holes that cannot be moved onto or through (even knights can't land there; sliders can't cross). Narrator dodges the Locust while it eats engine material (e.g. a trapped rook on a8). The final game ends in a draw by stalemate/blocked position after the Locust deletes key squares.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
After each full turn, 66% chance the Locust spawns on a uniformly random square (any square, occupied or empty).
The Locust is visible for one turn as a warning; at the end of the next full turn it deletes the square and any piece on it, then vanishes.
Deleted squares are permanent holes: no piece may move onto them and sliding pieces cannot pass over them ('it would simply fall through').
If a king is evaporated that side loses [inferred].
While a Locust is active a new one does not spawn [inferred from 'disappearing and choosing a different victim'].
